items.title: 68098_Snub Mosley oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] That's exactly what they would have done. I know that guy, that was Harriman, he was a real bastard.

ctx.x: The guy at the Metropole, they tried to pull a fast one. We were pulling a lot of people away from the Metropole at one time and they offered me a job at the Metropole to come in there in the afternoon. I knew what they were going to do, I would have come out of there and they would have fired me after a month.
That's exactly what they would have done. I know that guy, that was Harriman, he was a real bastard.

That's what the idea was, because we were drawing too many people. I stayed in there from '55 to '60 and I was up at the--in '57 I went to the Windsor, up in the Catskills. I'd go up there for the summer and come back in the fall. I stayed at the Windsor for two years, '57 and '58 and '59 I went to Grossinger's. Then I came back to the Frolic. In fact, I did the Frolic until '60. Then in '60 I went to the Riviera, Rube Congris' Riviera, that was a wonderful, beautiful thing there. We really made a very rich man…
